newsitem.title: UK: Phillips takes Enron gas dispute to top UK court.
newsitem.headline: Phillips takes Enron gas dispute to top UK court.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum, Agip and British Gas have been granted leave to appeal to the House of Lords, the highest court in Britain, in their dispute over North Sea gas sales with Enron, a government statement said.
The move reversed a decision in Enron's favour on October 10 last year which had in turn reversed a decision in Philips' favour on May 9.
Phillips and its partners agreed in 1993 to sell Enron natural gas produced from ther Judy and Joanne fields in the North Sea's J-Block.
Sale of the gas was scheduled to run from a commissioning date of September 25 1996, or earlier if agreed.
But Enron declined to agree a commissioning date for commercial reasons, and told the producers it would not take delivery of gas before September 30 1998.
The legal dispute centres on whether this amounted to a breach of the agreement.
